lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Hang one weight on a spring, it stretches. Double the weight—it stretches twice as far!

lines.speaker: skeptic
lines.text: Scrambled Latin letters, Hooke? Explain your hidden law!

lines.speaker: hooke
lines.text: More stretch means more pullback—F equals minus k x!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Next, Hooke aimed his brass microscope at cork—and named those tiny honeycomb rooms 'cells'!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Warning: stretch past the elastic limit, and metal deforms forever.

lines.speaker: skeptic
lines.text: No! You snapped my watch spring!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Yet Hooke's tiny spiral hairspring tamed the pocket watch—shrinking clocks to fit your palm!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Car shocks, skyscrapers, even DNA coils today—all obey Robert Hooke's law.
